quote: We we have a whole program here where we can redo the roof as well.
stewart_read: This is actually the POSITIVE example the schema references (SESSION18_fcbf33c1 is cited by name in cross_sell_signals.roof_replacement_planned as the bridge-in-4-seconds exemplar). The rep catches the garage-roof-needs-redo detail and immediately connects it to Ion's in-house reroof program rather than treating it as a dead end.
coaching_implication: Use this clip as the internal model for other setters — this is the fast, clean version of the bridge. Worth flagging to the manager as a positive replay, not just a gap to fix.

stewart_read: Customer discloses a budget-billing number and immediately volunteers the real driver behind it — a $500 summer bill from pool usage. The rep captures the number but the reasoning below covers the flip question directly.
coaching_implication: See bill_anchor_audit for the full flip assessment — captured but not turned into forward-pulling leverage in the moment.

quote: Was that was that 500 bill, that's probably the highest, I'm assuming. Oh, that's the highest I've ever had. Period.
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a strong anchor — her own words, 'the highest I've ever had, period' — and the rep's response is 'Gotcha' and a move to the next verify item. This was a natural spot to reflect the number back as a hook for the design call (e.g., tying the appointment to seeing what that number could look like with solar).
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be deliberately saving the number to let the closer use it fresh rather than pre-litigating it. Rejected — the rep never revisits or references the $500 figure again at any point in the call, including at booking or button-up, so there is no evidence of a deliberate hold for later use; the number was simply filed and not used.
coaching_implication: Coach the reflex: when a customer gives you an emotionally loaded number unprompted, mirror it back briefly ('that's a big jump — that's exactly the kind of number the design call will show you options against') before moving on. Costs 5 seconds, creates pull toward the appointment.

quote: K. I'm in I'm in Walmart, and so I don't have any of my stuff.
stewart_read: Customer is mobile and away from home with no app installed. Rep pivots to walking her through the utility website on her phone and captures via text photo — this matches the schema's shopping_customer_protocol almost exactly.
coaching_implication: Another positive replay moment — rep didn't defer bill collection or waste time; adapted the format to the customer's real-time constraint and got the bill same-call.

quote: Oh, I might have to go somewhere else and buy Jack Daniels because they're out.
stewart_read: Customer goes off-topic mid-login-struggle (shopping list, boyfriend's favorite whiskey). Rep responds naturally ('What flavor does he usually get?') rather than steering back abruptly, which likely kept the tone light during a frustrating tech-friction stretch.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep let the call drift off-task for nearly a minute. Rejected as the primary read — the drift cost negligible time relative to the login struggle itself, and the rapport moment likely reduced friction-driven irritation rather than adding it.
coaching_implication: Not a coaching concern on this call; note only if off-topic drift becomes a pattern across other calls from this rep.

quote: I haven't got any text yet.
stewart_read: Minor technical friction during the photo-text handoff (wrong number confirmation, camera app confusion) but resolved within about a minute, well inside the schema's 2-minute pivot budget for tech friction.
coaching_implication: No action needed — friction was real but resolved fast; this is what the tech_friction_handling directive considers acceptable.

quote: Okay. So you don't come out and look and do all that?
stewart_read: Customer directly asks about the process/format of the next step. Rep answers clearly (phone first, site survey later if she likes the design) but the answer is purely informational — no anticipation-building language about what she'll see or why it'll be worth her hour.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is supported here: the appointment-setting and button-up sequence still follows this exchange (11AM booking, email/text logistics), so there was clear room to add a forward-pulling line about the design call itself before moving into scheduling mechanics.
coaching_implication: When a customer asks 'what happens next,' it's a free opening to build anticipation for the specific appointment ('we'll walk through what your options look like against that $500 summer bill') rather than just describing logistics.
